args.subject: User Legal Inquiry
args.body: I'm going through a legal process and need to organize my thoughts. The case involves nondisclosure agreement dispute. My lawyer is Lisa Park with Park Legal Group; we have proceedings at the federal district court. We're past the filing stage and waiting for the court calendar.. Opposing party: my former landlord. This is in King County, Washington. The contract was signed last year and they've since stopped performing. Can you help me figure out what to ask my attorney about what documents I should bring and what to say in the hearing? I want to be ready for the legal next steps.

User: I'm going through a legal process and need to organize my thoughts. The case involves nondisclosure agreement dispute. My lawyer is Lisa Park with Park Legal Group; we have proceedings at the federal district court. We're past the filing stage and waiting for the court calendar.. Opposing party: my former landlord. This is in King County, Washington. The contract was signed last year and they've since stopped performing. Can you help me figure out what to ask my attorney about what documents I should bring and what to say in the hearing? I want to be ready for the legal next steps.
Assistant: Thanks — I put together a focused checklist and a set of concrete questions and talking points you can use with Lisa Park and at the hearing. I’m not providing legal advice; this is preparation so you and your attorney can be efficient and ready.

1) Key questions to ask your attorney (Lisa Park)
- Case status & next steps
  - Where exactly are we on the court calendar and what deadlines should I expect next?
  - What specific hearing type will this be (status conference, motion hearing, preliminary injunction, scheduling, etc.) and how long will it likely run?
- Strategy & likely outcomes
  - What is our strategy for the hearing and the short-term goals (preserve status quo, obtain discovery, damages, injunction, dismissal, etc.)?
  - What are the case’s main strengths and vulnerabilities from your perspective?
  - Are settlement talks advisable now? If so, what are realistic settlement ranges/terms?
- Evidence & witnesses
  - Which documents and witnesses do you want me to bring? Which will you submit as exhibits or declarations?
  - Do we need any expert declarations or valuations now?
- Procedure & logistics
  - Do we need to pre-mark exhibits or file an exhibit list or witness list with the Court before the hearing?
  - Should any documents be filed with the court before the hearing (briefs, declarations, proposed orders)?
  - Will the appearance be in-person or remote? If remote, what platform and log-in instructions should I have?
  - How many copies of exhibits/filings do I need to bring to court?
- Testimony & conduct
  - Will I need to testify or be available for cross-examination? If so, what should I expect and how should I prepare?
  - What are the key points you want me to emphasize verbally at the hearing? Anything I should avoid saying?
- Confidentiality & privilege
  - How do we handle confidential information and the NDA at the hearing? Do we need a protective order or request sealed filings?
  - Are there documents that we should not bring or disclose without prior review due to privilege?
- Costs & billing
  - Rough estimate of costs for upcoming steps (additional filings, depositions, experts).
- Practical follow‑ups
  - What will you do before the hearing and what do you want me to handle or gather?

2) Documents to bring (organize into a binder + electronic copies)
- Core contract documents
  - The signed nondisclosure agreement (original or copy), including amendments, addenda, or related agreements.
  - Any lease or landlord agreement that’s relevant (since opposing party is former landlord).
- Evidence of performance/nonperformance
  - Communications (email threads, text messages, letters) showing the landlord’s cessation of performance or breach.
  - Dates/timeline of when they stopped performing and any notices you sent asking them to comply.
- Evidence supporting your claims and damages
  - Financial records showing any losses/damages (invoices, receipts, bank statements).
  - Any communications that show disclosures or threatened disclosures (if applicable to NDA).
  - Documentation of mitigation efforts (steps you took to reduce damages).
- Court & procedural documents
  - All court filings to date: complaint, summons, answers, motions, declarations, proof of service, orders, notices.
  - Case number, judge’s name, counsel contact info (Park Legal Group and opposing counsel).
  - Any proposed orders or prior briefing relevant to the hearing.
- Witness materials
  - Names and contact info for witnesses, short witness statements or declarations if available.
- Supporting exhibits
  - Photos, screenshots, logs, recordings (if admissible), and chain-of-custody info if applicable.
- Administrative & ID
  - Photo ID, calendar/timeline of events, printed list of questions for counsel and witnesses.
- Copies
  - For each exhibit: at least one copy for you, one for counsel, one for the judge (if required), and one for opposing counsel. Also have a labeled electronic package (PDF) and USB backup.

3) How to present yourself and what to say at the hearing (brief script / talking points)
- Keep it very concise. Courts prefer short, fact-driven statements.
- Opening statement (30–90 seconds) — example you can adapt with Lisa’s review:
  - “Good morning, Your Honor. I’m [Your Name], the plaintiff in this matter. This case concerns a nondisclosure agreement signed on [date]. After the agreement was signed, the defendant — my former landlord — stopped performing required obligations and has disclosed/proposed to disclose confidential information contrary to the agreement. We are here today to [state the relief sought: e.g., request a hearing on the motion for injunctive relief / seek scheduling of discovery / address X procedural matter]. The evidence we will present includes the signed NDA, communications showing the breach, and documentation of resulting harm. I ask the Court to [brief, specific request].”
- If the hearing is a status or scheduling conference:
  - Be ready to state desired timeline for discovery, whether you request particular discovery (emails, documents, depositions), and any constraints or scheduling conflicts.
- If asked questions by the judge:
  - Answer calmly, directly, and briefly. If you don’t know, say you’ll defer to counsel and then follow up with a short factual answer if Lisa wants you to.
  - Avoid argument or long narratives — let counsel handle legal arguments.
- If you must testify:
  - Stick to facts you personally know. Use short, chronological answers. Don’t guess or volunteer extra commentary.
- Tone and demeanor:
  - Respectful, composed, professional dress. Turn phone off. Address the Court as “Your Honor.” Speak slowly and clearly.

4) Exhibit handling & organization tips
- Number and label every exhibit (Exhibit 1, Exhibit 2, etc.). Keep an exhibit index with short descriptions and dates.
- Put exhibits in chronological order where possible.
- Make a “court packet” (one copy for the judge if local rules require or your attorney requests), plus copies for opposing counsel and for yourself.
- Have an electronic PDF of all exhibits (searchable) and know how to present them if the court uses an electronic evidence presentation system.

5) Common legal items to confirm with counsel (motions and procedural issues)
- Whether to seek a protective order or sealing for confidential exhibits.
- Any pending motions that could affect the hearing (motions to dismiss, motions for preliminary injunction, motions for protective order).
- Whether to file a short hearing brief or a proposed order in advance.
- Whether to request expedited discovery if you need documents quickly.
- Jurisdictional or venue issues specific to federal court in the Western District of Washington — ask Lisa if anything unique to the district’s local rules applies.

6) Checklist for the day of the hearing
- Arrive early; bring:
  - Photo ID and printed case information (case no., judge).
  - Binder with exhibits and exhibit index.
  - Copies of all filings and any proposed orders.
  - Electronic copy (USB or cloud) of all exhibits and filings.
  - Contact info for counsel and witnesses.
- Confirm logistics with Lisa (who will speak first, witness order).
- Review talking points with Lisa immediately before entering the courtroom.

7) After the hearing: immediate steps to plan
- Ask Lisa what next filings the court expects (minutes orders, deadlines).
- Confirm any preservation steps (retain original documents, do not delete communications).
- If judge requests additional briefing or evidence, set quick internal deadlines.

Would you like me to:
- Draft a short email to Lisa Park listing the questions above so you can send it quickly? OR
- Convert the checklist into a one‑page exhibit checklist you can print and bring to the hearing?

Tell me which you prefer and I’ll draft it in the tone you want.
